DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY

Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), Treasury.

31 CFR Chapter X, Part 1010

Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Involving MEXC

Global

AGENCY: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), Treasury.

ACTION: Order.

SUMMARY: FinCEN is issuing notice of an order, pursuant to section 9714(a) of the

Combating Russian Money Laundering Act (Public Law 116-283), as amended by section

6106(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Public Law 117-81),

finding that MEXC Global—including any of its subsidiaries, branches, and offices, as well as

any successor entities, operating in any jurisdiction outside of the United States—is a financial

institution operating outside of the United States of primary money laundering concern in

connection with Russian illicit finance and prohibiting certain transmittals of funds involving

MEXC Global.

DATES: This action is effective [INSERT 30 DAYS AFTER THE DATE OF

PUBLICATION IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].

Page 2
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: FinCEN’s Regulatory Support Section by

submitting an inquiry at www.fincen.gov/contact.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

     I.   Summary of Order

          As set out in this order, MEXC Global has facilitated funds transfers by Russia-affiliated

illicit actors and in connection with other Russia-associated illicit activities, including sanctions

evasion, and activity facilitated by Russian darknet markets. It has also facilitated billions of

dollars in transactions benefitting Iran and its proxies, financial facilitators of the Democratic

People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK), and other cybercrime actors. Accordingly, this order (1)

sets forth FinCEN’s determination that MEXC Global, a convertible virtual currency (CVC)

exchanger, along with any subsidiaries, branches, and offices of MEXC Global, and any

successor entities, operating in any jurisdiction outside of the United States (collectively, MEXC

Global)1 is a financial institution operating outside of the United States of primary money

laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance; and (2) prohibits certain

transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global, by any covered financial institution.

    II.   Background

(Secretary) “determines that reasonable grounds exist for concluding that one or more financial

          B. MEXC Global

          MEXC Global is a CVC exchanger founded in 2018 that is incorporated in the

Seychelles, without a virtual asset service provider license9 and operates in and across over 170

countries10 through an array of current or former subsidiaries, branches, and offices, including,

but not limited to, MEXC Global Ltd and MX Global Ltd in Seychelles; MEXC Estonia OÜ in

Estonia; GIDA Technology AG in Switzerland; MXC Global Ltd in the United Kingdom; and,

formerly, Singapore-registered MEXC Global Foundation Ltd and MEXC Singapore Pte Ltd.11

          As of June 2026, MEXC Global processed more than USD 1 billion in daily transactions,

while maintaining approximately USD 5 billion in reserve assets. As such, MEXC Global is

among the 20 largest CVC exchangers in the world by trading volume.12 As of December 2025,

MEXC Global commanded approximately nine percent of the global market share of centralized

III.    Finding that MEXC Global is a Financial Institution Operating Outside the United
        States that is of Primary Money Laundering Concern in Connection with Russian
        Illicit Finance

        Based on public and non-public information available to FinCEN, FinCEN finds that

reasonable grounds exist for concluding that MEXC Global is a financial institution of primary

money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance—namely, through its

facilitation of funds transfers by Russia-affiliated illicit actors and in connection with other

Russia-associated illicit activities, including sanctions evasion, and activity facilitated by Russian

darknet markets. Moreover, FinCEN assesses that, in addition to facilitating Russian illicit

finance, MEXC Global has, in parallel, facilitated billions of dollars in transactions benefitting

Iran and its proxies, financial facilitators of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK),

and other cybercrime actors.

identified in 31 U.S.C. 5318A(c)(2)(B), taking into account the specific circumstances of money

         A. MEXC Global is a Financial Institution Operating Outside the United States

has long defined that term to include “money transmitters,” including persons that accept and

transmit value that substitutes for currency, such as CVC.17 MEXC Global, in operating as a

CVC exchanger, is a “money transmitter” because it is engaged in the transfer of funds or value

that substitutes for currency.18

throughout the world—over time maintaining, for instance, subsidiaries, branches, and offices in

Seychelles, Hong Kong, Singapore, Estonia, and the United Kingdom—and offers a range of

         Notably, to the extent that MEXC Global maintains or otherwise operates through

affiliates, subsidiaries, branches, or offices in the United States, this order expressly excludes all

such affiliates, subsidiaries, branches, or offices from the definition of “MEXC Global” and,

accordingly, such affiliates, subsidiaries, branches, or offices are outside the scope of this order.

         B. Finding That MEXC Global is a Financial Institution of Primary Money
            Laundering Concern in Connection with Russian Illicit Finance

         While MEXC Global’s anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism

(AML/CFT), customer identification and verification (sometimes referred to as “Know Your

Customer” or “KYC” information), and other due diligence processes20 prohibit, on paper, the

opening of accounts by individuals in certain jurisdictions, FinCEN assesses that, based on

public and non-public information, MEXC Global has facilitated transactions involving those

prohibited jurisdictions. In addition, MEXC Global has facilitated transactions involving Russia-

affiliated illicit actors and associated illicit activities, including sanctions evasion, and activity

facilitated by Russian darknet markets, as well as transactions involving not only U.S.-,

European Union-, and United Kingdom-sanctioned persons working on behalf of Iran and its

proxies and the DPRK, but also an array of cybercrime actors.

transactions in violation of its own user agreement, including direct transactions between MEXC

注51：II.Aの通り、第9714条の措置には、(1)31 U.S.C.5318A(b)の措置（米対象金融機関への記録保存・情報収集・報告義務の追加、外国銀行のためのコルレス等口座開設・維持への条件を含む）と、(2)資金送金の禁止・条件付与がある。

## 21ページ

〔前頁から継続〕例えば伝統的な銀行関係の外での資金移動は、他の外国金融機関との間接的なコルレス関係を通じて同社に米ドルへのアクセスを許し得る。
D. 禁止措置を命令・規則のどちらで課すか
第9714条により長官は送金禁止を含む一つ以上の特別措置を『命令、規則その他法が認める方法』で課せる。FinCENは根底にある脅威の性質を考え、命令と規則を比較した。同社が取引・資金アクセスを仲介する不正行為者の差し迫った脅威、およびロシアの不正金融関連の疑わしい活動の取引を同社が処理し続けていることから、命令による対応が最適と判断した。また本命令は金融機関へ不当な負担や新しい・特殊な遵守費用を課さないと評価する。
本命令の写しは官報へ掲載される。MEXC Globalその他の関係者は、本命令に関係する情報を www.fincen.gov/contact でFinCENに提出できる。
V. 大統領令14294
同令第5条は、違反が刑事上の規制犯罪となり得る将来の規則制定案通知（NPRM）および最終規則を官報掲載する際、それが刑事規制犯罪である旨と根拠法令を特定する記述を含めるよう指示する〔次頁へ継続〕。

## 22ページ

〔前頁から継続〕大統領令14294は、その記述を司法省と協議して起草するよう当局へ指示する。〔注52〕
さらに、2025年5月9日以降に官報掲載される、刑事上の効果があるすべてのNPRM・最終規則の規制本文について、刑事規制犯罪の各構成要件ごとに主観的要件を明示し、根拠法令の関連条項を引用するよう指示する。
本命令の最終規定への故意の違反には、31 U.S.C.5322および31 CFR第X章の規則に基づく刑事制裁が科され得る。同法5322(a)、(b)の刑事責任の根拠は故意を構成要件として求める。第X章の規制違反に対する刑事制裁を定める既存31 CFR1010.840も故意要件を含む。この記述の起草に際しFinCENは司法省と協議した。
VI. 命令
A. 定義
1. MEXC Global
セーシェルを拠点とするCVC交換業者MEXC Globalの定義には、米国外の法域で金融機関として営業する支店、子会社、事務所と、その後継法人を含む。後継法人とは、資産の全部・一部を取得し、または新しい名称でMEXC Globalの業務を継続することによって、同社や支店・子会社・事務所に代わる者を意味する。これには本命令で米国外で金融機関として営業する同社の支店等と記述する法人を含むが、これらに限らない〔次頁へ継続〕。
注52：大統領令14294『連邦規制における過度の犯罪化への対処』90 FR20367（2025年5月9日発令、同月14日官報掲載）。https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/14294 。

当該ページに印字された参照URL（リンク先を今回取得済みとはしない）：
https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/14294

## 23ページ

〔前頁から継続〕米国内に所在するMEXC Globalの支店、子会社、事務所は、本命令上のMEXC Globalの定義から明示的に除外する。
2. 交換可能な仮想通貨
CVCとは、通貨と同等の価値を持つか通貨の代替として機能するが法定通貨の地位を持たない交換手段をいう。ビットコインは少なくとも一法域で法定通貨の地位があるものの、本命令上はCVCの一種に含める。
3. 対象金融機関
31 CFR1010.100(t)の金融機関と同じ意味とする。
4. 資金送金
CVCを含む資金の送付と受領を意味する。疑義を避けるため、本条では1010.100(ddd)の定義ではなく、この資金送金の定義を適用する。
5. その他の用語
本命令で別段定義されない用語は31 CFR第X章および31 U.S.C.5312の意味とする。
B. MEXC Global関連資金送金の禁止
対象金融機関は、MEXC Globalから、またはMEXC Globalへのいかなる資金送金も行うことを禁止する。

## 24ページ

C. 命令の期間
本命令の条項は［官報掲載日から30日後の日付を挿入］に発効し、終了日は設けない。
D. 権限の留保
FinCENは、MEXC Globalから、または同社への特定送金に条件を課し、本命令の義務に適切な適用除外を認める権限を留保する。
E. その他の義務
本命令のいかなる規定も、対象金融機関が銀行秘密法に基づき負う要件・義務（疑わしい取引報告SARの提出を含むがこれに限らない）、または米財務省OFACが運用・執行する制裁等の他の適用法規に基づく義務を、変更・損傷その他の形で影響するものと解釈してはならない。
F. 不遵守の制裁
対象金融機関とその役員、取締役、従業員、代理人は、本命令に故意に違反した場合、31 U.S.C.5321および5322に基づく民事・刑事制裁の責任を負い得る。
G. 命令の有効性
本命令のある条項を無効とする司法判断は、他の条項の有効性に影響せず、それらは引き続き完全な効力を持つ。

           In reaching its finding that MEXC Global is a financial institution operating outside the

United States of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance,

FinCEN considered the extent to which MEXC Global is used for legitimate business purposes.44
